The problem: JUnit assertions usage is wrong. In JUnit 5 (org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions), the overloads are assertNotNull(Object actual, String message) (message last) not first. Actually the signature is assertNotNull(T actual, String message) where message is second param. Wait compile error: it says no method assertNotNull(String, Message). They passed message first then actual. So need to swap order. Similarly for assertTrue(boolean condition, String message) and assertEquals(expected, actual, String message) but they used message first. So fix all assertions: change order to (actual, message) for assertNotNull and assertTrue? Actually assertTrue(boolean condition, String message). They used assertTrue(message, condition). So swap.

Also assertEquals(expected, actual, message). They used assertEquals(message, expected, actual). So swap.

assertNotEquals(message, expected, actual) also swap.

assertFalse(boolean condition, String message) swap.

assertNull(Object actual, String message) swap.

Thus modify test code accordingly.

Also there is a CsvSource line: "'., true'" maybe missing quote? They have "'., true'" but zone string '.' maybe root zone? Should be "'.', true"? Actually they intend root zone '.' but Name.root maybe. Not compile error.

Also CsvSource list: they have comment lines inside array; but syntax: @CsvSource({ // root zone ... "'example.com.', true", "'sub.domain.example.org.', true", "'., true'" }) There's a stray comment inside braces; but Java allows comments. The third entry "'., true'" missing closing quote after '.'? It is "'., true'" which is a string literal starting with ', then . , then space true'?? Actually it's a single string literal: "'., true'"? Wait they have single quotes inside double quotes? They wrote "'., true'". That's a double-quoted string? No they used single quotes to wrap each CSV value? In CsvSource, each entry is a string, like "'example.com.', true". That's fine: the outer braces contain strings. So "'., true'" is a string containing . and true? It is "'., true'" (double quotes surrounding). That's okay.

Thus only assertion order errors.

Also import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.* provides overloads.

Let's produce corrected code.
